name: Pherkad Minor
description: A star 134 parsecs away, 30 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74793: radius 29.569 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 257.257 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.106) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74793: effective temperature 4254 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.044)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74793: distance 133.864 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.088), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 134 parsecs away, 30 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 257 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,254 K, so 29.569 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 74793: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 11 Ursae Minoris
quotes.card: 11 Ursae Minoris, formally named Pherkad Minor, is a single star located approximately 410 light-years away in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.
quotes.introduction: The star is visible to the naked eye as a faint, orange-hued star with an apparent visual magnitude of 5.15.
